correctness.rationale: Under an ideal rank-(B-mN) spectral preconditioner, independent real Gaussian quadratic forms have zero bias and MSE F_N=(2/N)sum_{i>B-mN}log^2(1+lambda_i) by the exact chi-square second moment. Grouping ordered squared log-eigenvalues into nondecreasing blocks c_j gives F_(N+1)-F_N=2H_N/[N(N+1)] and H_(N+1)-H_N=(N+1)(c_(N+2)-c_(N+1))>=0, with H_N=N*c_(N+1)-sum_{i>B-mN}a_i. All nondivisible budget, zero, tied-spectrum and boundary cases are covered. Finite geometric series establish q^(-m)+q^(n-B+m)>=2 for the entire one-probe optimality region. Verified from the packaged verify.py using 3261 exact-rational allocation cases, 15198 values and 108 geometric cases; these are supplemental to the algebra.

originality.rationale: Cortinovis and Toni 2026 Sec. 2 equations (14) and (15) give the exact MSE for any individual ideal allocation and a comparison against one probe for each fixed allocation. They are credited, not claimed as new. The present theorem proves a global single-crossing structure across the complete integer budget range, exact reduction of all one-probe comparisons to the adjacent two-probe comparison, precise tie conditions, and sharp geometric-log-spectrum optimal allocation count; the inspected source does not state these. Residual risk: the structural lemma is short, derives from a source-known MSE expression, and an older equivalent result may exist.
residual_risks: Source equation (14) already gives every individual MSE and source equation (15) permits exhausting all allocations. Novelty rests on the new spectral monotonicity reduction and geometric phase rather than a new error formula.
An equivalent optimizer single-crossing argument might exist in trace estimation or optimal experimental design under different notation; search is not an exhaustiveness proof.
Hutch++ original manuscript not fully inspected; publisher abstract concerns a distinct worst-case model, and a buried exact-allocation special case cannot be categorically excluded.
The known-spectrum idealization is not an oracle-free implementable procedure; variance-optimal modeled charges need not minimize actual run time.

value.rationale: The paper motivating the finding recommends a single Gaussian sample for moderate/rapid spectral decay and develops an adaptive alternative for slow decay. Determining whether that one probe is globally MSE-optimal, not just better than a particular split, is a natural exact resource-allocation problem. The theorem classifies all integer allocation counts including ties and shows just one adjacent oracle check is necessary/sufficient, while the exact geometric threshold q^m=1/2 and flat-spectrum opposite extreme connect spectral decay to the optimal strategy. It is a natural complete classification under the precise ideal model rather than an arbitrary parameter enumeration. Practical limitation is that unknown spectrum is not cheaply revealed.
